title: Does a hallucination probe trained on one domain transfer to a very different domain?

original_idea.body: Train a linear hallucination probe on one domain, evaluate zero-shot on OOD long-form sets (medical/legal), and compare cross-domain AUC to in-domain AUC and a semantic-entropy baseline.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: cross-domain hallucination monitoring is useful but link to catastrophic AI risk skips a step.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Linear probe trained on one domain, tested OOD; public datasets.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable (cross-domain AUC vs in-domain and baseline).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: High-stakes domains where labs lack data, open tooling.

novelty.reasoning: Hallucination probes well-studied; cross-domain transfer may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: This cross-domain high-stakes test may be open.
